\section*{Question 4}

Let \(f\) be a function defined on the closed interval \(-3 \leq x \leq 4\) with \(f(0)=3\). The graph of \(f^{\prime}\), the derivative of \(f\), consists of one line segment and a semicircle, as shown above.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] On what intervals, if any, is \(f\) increasing? Justify your answer.
\item[(b)] Find the \(x\)-coordinate of each point of inflection of the graph of \(f\) on the open interval \(-3<x<4\). Justify your answer.
\item[(c)] Find an equation for the line tangent to the graph of \(f\) at the point (0, 3).
\end{itemize}
![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/f868c3ef-fbbe-4582-b51b-a9bbf3daf124-1.jpg?height=430&width=610&top_left_y=385&top_left_x=1384)
\begin{itemize}
\item[(d)] Find \(f(-3)\) and \(f(4)\). Show the work that leads to your answers.
\item[(a)] The function \(f\) is increasing on [-3,-2] since \(f^{\prime}>0\) for \(-3 \leq x<-2\).
\item[(b)] \(x=0\) and \(x=2\)
\(f^{\prime}\) changes from decreasing to increasing at \(x=0\) and from increasing to decreasing at \(x=2\)
\item[(c)] \(f^{\prime}(0)=-2\)
Tangent line is \(y=-2 x+3\).
\item[(d)]
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(0)-f(-3) & =\int_{-3}^{0} f^{\prime}(t) d t \\
& =\frac{1}{2}(1)(1)-\frac{1}{2}(2)(2)=-\frac{3}{2}
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
f(-3)=f(0)+\frac{3}{2}=\frac{9}{2}
\]
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(4)-f(0) & =\int_{0}^{4} f^{\prime}(t) d t \\
& =-\left(8-\frac{1}{2}(2)^{2} \pi\right)=-8+2 \pi
\end{aligned}
\]
\[
f(4)=f(0)-8+2 \pi=-5+2 \pi
\]
\end{itemize}
